Eleven comments

Composed by Martin Wynne. I find the sequence of triplets in the turn of the tune very satisfying to play.

↳ Posted by radriano on December 20th, 2001.

I knew this tune But I didn’t know it was one of Martin’s. I learned it from a tape of Brian Conway, great tune.

↳ Posted by b.maloney on December 20th, 2001.

This is the “Martin Wynne’s” that’s on Trian II.

↳ Posted by JSC_from_IL on September 15th, 2003.

Martin Wynnes #4

This is a copy/paste from sessioneer.org where it’s called Martin Wynne’s # 4.

↳ Posted by edl on June 1st, 2008.

Martin Donohue’s CD “Tasty Touches” has a set of 4 Martin Wynne’s reels, finishing with this one. With Brian Conway on fiddle and Brendan Dolan on piano.

↳ Posted by Tony O'Rourke on June 24th, 2014.

Martin Wynne’s, X:3

Here’s a setting from Liam Kelly and Philip Duffy recording Sets in Stone. Lovely playing. Great tune!

↳ Posted by jdicarlo on April 18th, 2017.

Martin Wynne’s, X:4

Heard from the playing of Oisín Mac Diarmada (at a workshop).

↳ Posted by Ian Varley on November 27th, 2019.

Martin Wynne’s, X:5

for flute, pipes, tin whistle

↳ Posted by UPipes & harp on November 1st, 2023.

Martin Wynne’s, X:6

A flute version from Mike McGoldrick’s Arc album, third tune in a set on the Bb flute with some folding over the fiddle in the first part.

↳ Posted by Alex Davidson on March 18th, 2026.

Martin Wynne’s, X:7

A-flat version from Carlos Sweeney McCartin.

↳ Posted by spraff on July 7th, 2026.

Re: Martin Wynne’s

For the future, transcribing at pitch isn’t really very useful - it would be better to transpose this into G (which is how the music is actually played on instruments tuned up to E flat/D sharp).

↳ Posted by Sláine on July 7th, 2026.
